author: ansel_grieco
subject: Fallowmere is moving high school start to 8:45, and I say it's about time
body: The board voted 5 to 2 to push Fallowmere High's start to 8:45 next fall, and I say it's about time. Teenagers have been sleeping through first period for a decade, and the sleep study the district cited is not a close call. The parents complaining about after-school jobs and buses should read the study before the next election. Nobody likes change, but the kids don't get a vote.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Nobody asked the bus drivers, and I'd bet nobody asked the ones who run the six o'clock route either. Pass.

comments.author: ansel_grieco
comments.body: The board did ask. There were three public hearings, Dale, and you didn't show up to any of them.

comments.author: henrik_dahl
comments.body: The staff memo puts the new bus contract at about 1.3 million dollars a year, and the sleep study sampled 400 students. I'd like to see the full math before we celebrate.

comments.author: wendell_pike
comments.body: It was Board Resolution 26-09, item 4 on the August agenda, and the minutes are posted on the district site. The vote was 5 to 2, with the two no votes citing transportation costs.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: My teen is up at 5:30 for swim, so a later start helps, but the real problem is after-practice rides. Can the district add a late bus for the sports kids?

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Sleep matters on the road too. I've worked too many crashes at seven in the morning involving drowsy teens, so I'm for the later start.

comments.author: leona_brooks
comments.body: Fine, but an 8:45 start means school zone traffic will be jammed at three in the afternoon, so somebody needs to fix the road before the bell.

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Anyone who thinks a seven o'clock bus is too early is spoiled and has clearly never worked a day in their life. Grow up.

author: priya_lakhani
subject: Ladder Tutoring Works helped my son with fractions
body: Our son was stuck on fractions all spring, and after six weeks at Ladder Tutoring Works on Brisco Avenue his grade went from a D to a B-plus. His tutor sends a short note after every session that says exactly what to practice at home. It isn't cheap, but they had summer openings and the sessions are only 45 minutes. Thank you to whoever mentioned them to me in the spring, it really did help.

comments.author: remy_castellano
comments.body: Do they do early reading too? My four-year-old is starting to ask about letters.

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: They have a reading track for kindergarten and first grade. Ask for the intake call, not the web form, because the calls get answered faster. Thanks!

comments.author: samir_qureshi
comments.body: Is the price per session or per package? We're looking at a few options for our daughter.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: Bluebird Hollow runs an after-school homework hour, and a few of their kids went to Ladder over the summer with good results. Sign-ups fill fast at both, so book early.

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: A package is cheaper per session, and they'll let you pause it for a month. I'd ask for the six-week block. Thanks!

author: deb_halvorsen
subject: Free flu shot clinic at Calloway Community Hall, Saturday 9 to noon
body: The county health team is running a free flu shot clinic at the Calloway Community Hall this Saturday from 9 to noon, and no appointment is needed. Bring your insurance card if you have one, but it's free either way. Bring a list of your medications so the nurses can check for interactions, and wear a short-sleeve shirt. Ask the nurses which version of the vaccine fits your kids, because it depends on age.

comments.author: lena_hoffer
comments.body: Hi, I'm new and I don't have a car. Is there a bus that stops near the Community Hall?

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: Route 6 stops a block away at Pell and Calloway, and the drivers know the hall. Walk-ins are fine, but the line is shorter before ten.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Thank you, Deb! I'm bringing my mother-in-law, she has a list of pills as long as my arm. Will they do the shot for seniors too?

comments.author: ngozi_adeyemi
comments.body: Night shift nurse here. Drink water the day before and eat breakfast, since that helps the lightheaded folks, and bring the med list.

comments.author: vivian_oduya
comments.body: Thank you for posting this. I'm pregnant, so is it okay to attend, or should I call my doctor first?

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: Yes, the flu shot is recommended in pregnancy and the nurses are trained for it. It's still worth a call to your own doctor about the other shots.

author: kayleigh_drummond
subject: Urgent care on Velder or the ER for a toddler's ear infection?
body: My son has had a fever of 102 since last night and his ear is really hurting, he's three. Is the new Pellworth Urgent Care on Velder Street worth it at eight at night, or should we just go to the ER? I don't want to waste our money, but I also don't want to sit for six hours. Did anyone go there last week?

comments.author: ngozi_adeyemi
comments.body: Urgent care is fine for an ear infection with a fever. Go to the ER if he's hard to wake, has a stiff neck, or keeps throwing up.

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: Call Pellworth before you leave and ask about the wait. They take walk-ins until nine, and the front desk will tell you how long the line is.

comments.author: kayleigh_drummond
comments.body: Thank you, that's a relief. Should I give him Tylenol before we go, and how do I know the right dose for his weight?

comments.author: remy_castellano
comments.body: My son had the same thing in the spring, and urgent care took forty minutes. Weigh him first and read the dose on the box, the pharmacist can double-check it.

comments.author: benito_ruiz
comments.body: There's construction on Velder by Sayer Lane, so take the back road from the north side. Parking is around the back.

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Sending good wishes to your little guy. Let us know how it goes, and I'll bring soup on Thursday if you need it.

author: remy_castellano
subject: Pediatrician recommendations? Our insurance changed
body: We're looking for a pediatrician for our two toddlers, and the practice we used before stopped taking our insurance this year. Does anyone have a doctor who is patient with anxious parents? I'd also love a dentist who does kids, because the last one made my oldest cry for an hour.

comments.author: kwame_ofori
comments.body: The pediatric group on Ilsted Way is good. My kids had their checkups there, and the front desk is patient about phone calls.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Lindqvist Family Dental took my two last spring, and they're gentle with little ones, with a sticker chart at the chair. They see kids on Fridays, so ask for a Friday slot.

comments.author: renata_ocampo
comments.body: Ask the pediatric group which pharmacy they use, and tell them you want Spanish forms if you need them. I'm happy to help translate.

comments.author: remy_castellano
comments.body: Thank you Lupe, Lindqvist is on my list! Do they take the state Medicaid plan? I'll call tomorrow.

comments.author: deb_halvorsen
comments.body: New patients usually need the immunization record, so bring the card and ask the pediatrician's office to fax it ahead. That saves a return visit.

author: lupe_ochoa
subject: Meal train for Hal, he's home from hip surgery and needs dinners
body: Hal Brenneman came home from hip surgery on Tuesday and isn't supposed to lift anything heavier than a coffee cup for six weeks. His daughter is driving in for two days, and after that it's on us. We're starting a meal train for weekday dinners, with the sign-up link in the comments, so please list allergies on anything you bring. If you can only do one night, that's a huge help.

comments.author: paulina_ferraro
comments.body: Hi, I'm new and I'd love to help. I can do Thursday with a lasagna. Is that okay with the allergy list?

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Count me in for Wednesday. I'm tagging Colleen so we can cover the weekend too.

comments.author: hal_brenneman
comments.body: Thank you all. The walker is the worst tool I've ever used, and I've used a lathe with a bent handle. Lupe, tell them not to bring two lasagnas.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: Lupe, I can take Hal to physical therapy on Tuesdays if his daughter is gone by then. Just message me the time and I'll be at the curb.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: Offering rides to the clinic for Hal, and I'm free every weekday after ten. Message me and we'll set it up.

comments.author: priya_lakhani
comments.body: Thank you for organizing this, Lupe. We'll bring Sunday dinner, and please tell Hal we're wishing him a smooth recovery. Thanks!

author: cyrus_mehta
subject: Severe thunderstorm warning until 3 a.m., power flickering on Dunmore
body: The weather service has a severe thunderstorm warning for us until 3 a.m., with quarter-size hail reported near the Vantage Creek bridge and gusts up to 70. The power has flickered twice on Dunmore, and the outdoor sirens sounded a few minutes ago. I've got the car in the garage and the basement lights on, but I'm up all night. If you have older neighbors, please check on them.

comments.author: dorothy_breen
comments.body: I'm so sorry, I'm new and a little scared. Is an interior bathroom safe if we don't have a basement?

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Pick the lowest interior room away from windows, put on shoes, and keep a flashlight by you. If the sirens go again, don't go outside to look.

comments.author: theo_marchetti
comments.body: New to town here. Is there an emergency shelter in Wren Hollow, or do we go to the school? I don't know where anything is yet.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: The shelter is the Community Hall on Ilsted Way, and the Ridgeline gym is the backup, per the county page. If the power is out and someone is in danger, call 911 first.

comments.author: imani_fairley
comments.body: Checking on my block now. The couple on Velder lost power, so I'm bringing them a flashlight and a battery radio.

comments.author: dale_hartwell
comments.body: Keep your car out of the street, because the storm drains on Dunmore back up in about twenty minutes and the water stays on the road.

comments.author: cyrus_mehta
comments.body: Dorothy, message me here if the lights go out, I'm up anyway. Asking was the right instinct.

author: ruben_villamizar
subject: Outdoor siren test is the first Wednesday at noon, please don't call 911
body: Reminder that the county runs the outdoor siren test at noon on the first Wednesday of each month, and the Calloway siren is the one on the water tower. It's a three-minute tone followed by a voice message saying it's only a test. Last time a lot of people called the non-emergency line, so please don't. The schedule is posted on the city's Public Safety page if you want to check it.

comments.author: shirin_bahrami
comments.body: Confirmed on the city's Public Safety page, noon on the first Wednesday of each month. Good to have it in writing.

comments.author: jolene_harkins
comments.body: I always forget and then I nearly drop my coffee. Thanks, Ruben, I'll set a reminder on the phone.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Good reminder. If you hear sirens on another day, don't wait, check your phone and the TV for the alert. The test is the only scheduled one.

comments.author: wade_tanaka
comments.body: Our kids cry at the siren, so we treat the test as a drill and head to the basement for a minute. Good practice for everyone.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: Agreed, Curtis. The sirens are for outside, so if you're inside with the TV on, you're listening for the alert.

author: fiona_rawlings
subject: Basement flooded after last night, water up to the second step
body: Our sump pump quit around two in the morning during the storm, and the basement took about two inches of water before we noticed. Anton and Renata came over with buckets, but the carpet is a loss and the dehumidifier runs nonstop. If your pump is more than ten years old, please test it tonight. Does anyone know a company that comes out on a Sunday?

comments.author: anton_pelc
comments.body: Sorry, Fiona. Bring a box fan from the hardware store, because drying the subfloor is what saves the drywall.

comments.author: brendan_doyle
comments.body: Check the discharge line outside, because a frozen or clogged pipe causes most pump failures. I give free estimates, but I'm not out on Sundays, so call Monday.

comments.author: ivan_kuzmenko
comments.body: Unplug the pump, lift out the float, and check that the check valve arrow points up toward the house. If the arrow is backwards, the water can't get out and the pump can't clear the line.

comments.author: samir_qureshi
comments.body: We had Bramwell Electric put a dedicated outlet on ours last month, and it's been fine since. They came out the same day.

comments.author: casey_ostrander
comments.body: I'm new and didn't know we had a sump pump. Where would I find it in a house like ours?

comments.author: fiona_rawlings
comments.body: Thanks Brendan. The pump is fourteen years old, so I'd guess that's the problem. I'll call on Monday.

author: ruth_ellery
subject: First frost last night in the Bend, cover your tomatoes next time
body: First frost hit the Bend last night, and the gauge in my garden read 31 degrees at five in the morning. The basil is done and the squash leaves are black, but the kale and leeks are fine. I'm not running to the store for row covers this late, but old bedsheets from the shed work in a pinch. Mulch your beds this week while the soil is still warm.

comments.author: ben_hollister
comments.body: Thanks Ruth, I'm new here. Should I pull the tomatoes now, or is there a trick to keeping them going a couple more weeks?

comments.author: ruth_ellery
comments.body: Pull the green ones and set them on a windowsill to ripen, they'll turn in about a week. Leave the peppers on another night, they're tougher than they look.

comments.author: theo_marchetti
comments.body: Does this mean I can start the garden bed I've been planning? I have no idea what zone we're in, so any advice would help.

comments.author: maribel_serrano
comments.body: The kids are begging for hot cocoa after the frost walk, so we'll be out in the Bend. Ruth, the mulch reminder is well timed.

comments.author: renata_ocampo
comments.body: Ruth, your kale is the envy of the Greaves Mill plots. Can I trade you seeds from the fall plot if you're saving any?

author: tomasz_wojcik
subject: Ice storm, trees down on Dunstan Road, anyone with power?
body: Freezing rain since four o'clock, with trees down across Dunstan Road near the old water tower and the power out on the east side of Wren Hollow. The city crew says about twelve hours, and the salt trucks aren't out yet, so drive slow. I have a generator and about forty gallons of gas. If you need a place to warm up, message me.

comments.author: curtis_bell
comments.body: Stay off the roads unless you must. If anyone sees a line down, keep thirty feet back and call 911 right away.

comments.author: kofi_mensah
comments.body: The Greaves Mill pavilion has a generator and the heat on. If you're without power, come warm up and charge your phone until the city gets back on.

comments.author: lupe_ochoa
comments.body: Tomasz, we have power on Velder, so I'll take anyone who needs a hot shower. Tell them to come to the back door.

comments.author: samir_qureshi
comments.body: Heads up, the Ember Fields lift station is out too, so don't run the washer or flush if you're on the east side.

comments.author: tomasz_wojcik
comments.body: Thanks Lupe. I'll send people your way if the east side stays dark.

comments.author: ruben_villamizar
comments.body: The ice has the Velder bridge closed, and the county page lists the detour. Use Tennant Pike instead.

comments.author: jolene_harkins
comments.body: Heard at the diner that all of Dunstan Road is out and the crew hasn't reached the transformer yet. I'd wait before going out.

author: bridget_mccourt
subject: Heat advisory through Thursday, and the splash pad is closed AGAIN
body: The heat advisory runs through Thursday with a heat index near 102 by mid-afternoon. The city shut the Ember Fields splash pad for a valve problem, the third time this summer, and the shade trees by the ball field are drying out. Check on anyone who lives alone, especially the older folks on Parrish Court, and keep your dog off the hot pavement.

comments.author: augustin_perrault
comments.body: Put a frozen towel on the back of your neck, and check the dog's paws by holding your hand on the sidewalk for ten seconds. If your hand hurts, so do theirs.

comments.author: jonah_fitch
comments.body: The Halsey Crossing pool stays open until eight if anyone needs it. Bring a towel, because the lot fills by four.

comments.author: casey_ostrander
comments.body: I'm new and didn't know about the splash pad. Is there a cooling center for people without air conditioning?

comments.author: bridget_mccourt
comments.body: Yes, the Fennimore branch library is open until nine, with air conditioning and water at the desk. Ask at the front and they'll tell you where the chairs are.

comments.author: esther_lund
comments.body: Thank you for looking out for the older folks. I'm on Parrish and doing fine, but I'll check on the two doors across the street.
